content: Patients experiencing food insecurity often rely on inexpensive, carbohydrate-dense foods due to limited financial resources. This dietary pattern can significantly increase their risk of hyperglycemia. Furthermore, irregular food intake associated with food insecurity can predispose these individuals to hypoglycemia, particularly if they are using sulfonylureas or insulin as part of their diabetes management. Healthcare providers should carefully account for these risks when developing treatment plans. It is also essential to connect these patients with food assistance programs to help stabilize their dietary patterns and improve their overall health outcomes.
